classification.difficultyReason: The clearing multiplier is supplied; students factor it to cancel denominators, expand, recognise that quadratic terms cancel, and check the linear solution against excluded values.

content.prompt: Solve the equation $\dfrac{3x}{x-1}-\dfrac{2x}{x+1}=\dfrac{x^2+10}{x^2-1}$ by first multiplying both sides of the equation by $x^2-1$.

answer.worked:
The denominators require $x\ne1,-1$. First multiply both sides by $x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)$.
$$\begin{align*}
(x^2-1)\left(\frac{3x}{x-1}-\frac{2x}{x+1}\right)&=(x^2-1)\frac{x^2+10}{x^2-1}\\
3x(x+1)-2x(x-1)&=x^2+10\\
3x^2+3x-2x^2+2x&=x^2+10\\
x^2+5x&=x^2+10\\
5x&=10\\
x&=2
\end{align*}$$
Since $2\ne1,-1$, this solution is valid.
